meta.title: Requirements register
meta.note: 'Owner-provided' rows restate the project brief; there is no official source for an owner's own requirement, so they are labelled as owner-provided rather than given a fabricated citation. Rows marked 'Official' carry the link to the government source the requirement is derived from.

requirements.requirement: Remove or repair the bathtub wastewater overflow trip lever, which is stuck in the concealed plumbing behind the wall.
Treat the overflow location as hard to access; opening drywall is a possible but non-preferred outcome.
Record that five or more licensed plumbers have already been unable to remove it from above without concern about damaging the concealed plumbing.
Reference photographs of the work area are pending; analysis is description-based until they arrive.
Above-tub removal is the preferred outcome if a provider can do it without damaging the concealed plumbing.
Below-tub access is the accepted fallback recommended by the plumbers consulted.
The space below the tub is a storage unit; below-floor work may require opening the drywall ceiling.
Any ceiling opening must be restored, and the restored finish should keep the concealed connections serviceable in future.
Replace the waste-and-overflow assembly as a unit if the linkage, drop cylinder or tee cannot be freed; adjust the linkage first if it can be.
Confirm the exact scope in writing for each quote: adjust only, lever/diverter, or full waste-and-overflow replacement.
Re-quote one identical scope across the shortlisted providers before comparing prices.
One accountable vendor must deliver both the plumbing work and the drywall opening and restoration.
The work must be performed by a licensed plumber or contractor; verify the licence number on CSLB before signing.
The licence must be current and active on the day the contract is signed.
Confirm workers'-compensation and liability coverage for whoever works in the unit.
Confirm the vendor services San Francisco.
Prefer vendors whose licence covers both trades, or who name their plumbing/drywall subcontractors in writing.
Confirm with the vendor which permit the work requires before it starts, and who pulls it.
Budget the official plumbing permit fee (Category 1P) separately from the quote.
Schedule the inspection before pipes are covered.
Give the tenant reasonable written notice stating date, approximate time and purpose of entry; 24 hours is presumed reasonable.
Keep entry within normal business hours unless the tenant consents otherwise.
Plan dust containment, protection or relocation of stored contents in the space below, and a water shut-off window.
Leak-test the new assembly before the ceiling is closed.
Photograph the existing condition, the opened cavity and the finished work for the record.
Obtain a written scope, price and schedule from the selected vendor before work starts.
Keep the three existing quotes as the budget baseline only — they are not a price range for one scope.
Obtain a combined plumbing-plus-drywall quote for the below-access fallback; none exists yet.
Publish every data row with a source link; leave unconfirmable values blank and flag them.
